title: Black images, NaN and grey mush

questions.q: What does SaveImage do with a pixel that is NaN?
options: Writes 0, which is black, and numpy logs a warning
questions.answer: Writes 0, which is black, and numpy logs a warning
questions.why: We ran it: pixels 0, 0, 0 and the warning invalid value encountered in cast.

questions.q: The latent's numbers look ordinary, but the image is black. Where do you look first?
questions.why: The latent came through fine, so the fault is after it. Try --fp32-vae.

questions.q: Why does a single NaN end up filling a tensor?
options: Each layer mixes neighbours, and any sum with NaN is NaN
It is a display effect only
questions.answer: Each layer mixes neighbours, and any sum with NaN is NaN
questions.why: The lab goes from 1 to 3072 NaN over 24 small convolutions.

questions.q: Why can fp16 give NaN where fp32 doesn't, on the same VAE?
options: fp16's largest value is 65504, so larger values become inf, and inf turns into NaN
questions.answer: fp16's largest value is 65504, so larger values become inf, and inf turns into NaN
questions.why: The model card says SDXL's activations are too big for fp16, and the lab shows the arithmetic.

questions.q: You use text to image with an empty latent and denoise 0.25. What should you expect?
options: Mush, since it starts from little noise with no picture underneath
questions.answer: Mush, since it starts from little noise with no picture underneath
questions.why: The lab: start sigma 0.231 of a possible 14.615. We state the look as an expectation, and did not render it.

questions.q: An SD 1.5 VAE is used on an SDXL latent. Why is there no error?
questions.why: The shapes fit, so nothing raises. The difference is in the scale and the learned space.
